benchmarks.title: Whole-blood eQTL classification
benchmarks.dataset: GTEx v10 whole-blood eQTLs; 14,811 positive variants and 1000 Genomes controls sampled at 10:1
benchmarks.method: An XGBoost classifier was trained on features derived from each model. The same chromosome-based train/test split was used for all methods, with about 20% of variants held out. This is supervised downstream classification, not a zero-shot comparison.
benchmarks.limitations: The study also evaluated GWAVA, which is not tracked here. Only the five tracked models and the AUROC values stated in the results text are shown. Model checkpoints were not specified in the main text. Training data overlap has not been independently assessed.

source.label: Chen et al. (2026), Results: eQTL identification

benchmarks.title: Putative causal eQTL classification
benchmarks.dataset: eQTL benchmark data from the Borzoi paper repository
benchmarks.method: A random forest was trained on model-derived differences between reference and alternate sequences. Results average three chromosome-held-out test sets. Enformer, Sei and AlphaGenome use output tracks; the language models use embeddings. Input lengths differ by model.
benchmarks.limitations: The paper also reports separate hidden-state and long-sequence configurations, which are excluded here. GROVER is not tracked. Model training overlap with this evaluation has not been independently assessed.

benchmarks.title: DNase I hypersensitivity classification
benchmarks.dataset: Human DNase I Hypersensitive sequence classification dataset
benchmarks.method: A supervised random forest was trained on mean-pooled embeddings from frozen pretrained models. Scores measure classification on the study's test set, not direct assay-track prediction.
benchmarks.limitations: GROVER was evaluated in the paper but is not tracked. Exact training overlap and uncertainty for this dataset have not been independently assessed.
